newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram says 7.0 pct growth feasible.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram says 7.0 pct growth feasible.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Friday the country can achieve annual economic growth of seven percent.
"India has reached a place where achieving seven percent growth was possible," Chidambaram said in reply to a question in the lower house of parliament.

President Shankar Dayal Sharma in a speech to parliament at the start of its budget session on Thursday also said the government's aim of achieving annual growth in gross domestic product (GDP) of at least seven percent over the next five years was feasible.
"But seven percent growth is not sufficient. There should be eight percent growth," Chidambaram said. "We should aim at eight percent and at the turn of the century it should reach nine percent."
The government estimates that GDP will expand by 6.8 percent in the 1996/97 fiscal year ending on March 31, compared with 7.1 percent in the previous year.
Chidambaram, a strong advocate of free-market policies, will spell out the government's economic blueprint on February 28 in the proposed budget for 1997/98 (April-March).
